reason: All explicitly named characters in this passage hold positions of authority or special status: Jonathan (יוֹנָתָן) is the prince and son of King Saul; Saul (שָׁאוּל) is the king himself; and Ahijah (אֲחִיָּה) is a priest serving as an ephod-bearer. The armor-bearer (נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו), who would arguably qualify as a regular person based on social status, is never given a proper name—he is identified only by his role. Thus, no character is both explicitly named with a proper name AND portrayed as an ordinary/regular person.
